external_matches.query_passage: Network operators generally adopt one of two business models. In the asset-owner model, the operator finances, builds and maintains the stations and earns revenue from electricity sales and usage fees. In the franchise model, site hosts such as retailers or fuel stations own the hardware and pay the network operator for software, billing services and roaming access. Revenue per station depends heavily on utilisation, and industry analysis suggests that most public stations require utilisation above fifteen percent to reach breakeven. Grid integration is a central planning concern. Unmanaged charging can coincide with evening demand peaks and force costly network upgrades, so utilities increasingly deploy smart-charging programmes that shift load to overnight periods or solar-rich hours. Recommendation We recommend the franchise model for the first sixty stations, with the asset-owner model reserved for three highway plazas where utilisation risk is lowest.
